ai.title: backend start script use ts-node
ai.summary: backend/package.json start script now runs ts-node src/server.ts. Original node dist/server.js renamed to start-js. common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts sendAction now returns result of sendMessage. Prevents server restarts while websocket connected.

eli5.text: When you type manicode and it connects to the server over a long-lived websocket, the connection now stays open instead of dropping and reconnecting. Behind the scenes, the server startup command was switched to a setup that compiles and runs the source code directly, and the message-sending step now reports back its result so callers can see whether it succeeded. The old startup method is still available under a separate name if needed.

ai.title: Add knowledge conciseness guidelines and strict file diff error
ai.summary: System prompt in backend/src/system-prompt.ts now enforces concise knowledge updates, integrating new info into existing sections rather than creating detailed minor-change sections. knowledge.md reflects this by stripping verbose descriptions from Main Components and Important Files. Backend prompts.ts replaces silent failure on missing file content with a thrown Error in processFileBlock, and reduces log noise by logging message counts instead of full payloads.

eli5.text: The assistant's notes about what it's learning and working on are now shorter and more focused, so instead of writing long, detailed updates it folds new information into existing sections. If the assistant tries to update a file it can't find, it now stops with a clear error instead of quietly doing nothing. Logs it produces now say how many messages it's seeing rather than dumping the full content of each message, making them easier to scan.

ai.title: Fix consecutive user messages in CLI chat
ai.summary: Refactored `manicode` in `src/index.ts` to extract `addUserMessage` helper. Fixes bug where consecutive user inputs were not properly merged if previous message lacked string content type check. Ensures `messageHistory` correctly appends to last user message or pushes new one. Scope limited to CLI chat history logic.

eli5.text: When you type several messages in a row during a chat, the assistant now correctly combines your latest message with any previous one you sent, instead of treating them as separate entries or dropping parts of your input. This fixes a glitch where consecutive messages from you were not properly merged unless your previous message was specifically checked for being plain text. The fix is live today in the chat history logic of the CLI interface.

ai.title: Agent persona named Manny; file-read loop guard
ai.summary: System prompt in backend/src/system-prompt.ts names the agent 'Manny' and adds friendly/professional traits. Replaced verbose 'Efficient File Reading' section with concise <important_instruction> block forbidding re-reading files before editing. Adds 'or you have recently read the file already' exception to initial read requirement.

eli5.text: The coding assistant now introduces itself as 'Manny' with a friendlier, more professional tone, making interactions feel less robotic and more welcoming. If you noticed the assistant's writing style and personality shifting to be warm and eager to help, that's because the change updated how the assistant presents itself in conversations. The assistant also got clearer instructions to avoid repeatedly reading the same file over and over, which keeps it from getting stuck in a loop.

ai.title: Refactor message schemas and disable file update user messages
ai.summary: Extracted `MessageContentObjectSchema` in `common/src/actions.ts` to simplify `MessageSchema` content union. In `src/index.ts`, commented out `addUserMessage` call triggered by file updates. Scope limited to core shared types and main entry logic. This temporarily suppresses automatic user message injection for file changes.

eli5.text: The assistant has stopped automatically posting a summary message in the chat when you edit a file, so you will no longer see an extra assistant note appear right after a file update. Behind the scenes, the developers also tidied up how the system validates the different types of messages, which does not change anything you see but makes future updates easier to manage. The change is live now, so if you save a file you should notice the missing automatic follow-up message.

ai.title: Add file reading loop prevention to system prompt
ai.summary: Added 'Efficient File Reading and Analysis' section to `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` to prevent agents from entering infinite loops by repeatedly reading the same files. Instructions now require checking conversation history for prior reads, planning file access logically, and summarizing gathered info before editing. Removed 'recently read' exception from edit pre-read rule in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` and deleted debug `console.log` from `backend/src/prompts.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant no longer wastes time re-reading files it has already looked at during a single task. Instead of jumping back to the same file over and over, it now keeps track of what it has seen, uses that memory to plan which files it actually needs next, and only re-reads a file right before editing it if it hasn't been read very recently. If you watched it work, you would notice it moving through files in a steadier, more purposeful order rather than cycling back to the same ones, and you would see it pause less on redundant reads. This behavior is live today across the backend tooling where the assistant operates.

ai.title: Rename assistant to Manny across system prompt, knowledge, and CLI
ai.summary: System prompt, knowledge.md, and src/index.ts replace generic 'assistant' references with 'Manny'. backend/src/system-prompt.ts adds conditional read_files logic for recently read files. knowledge.md documents Claude AI as Manny's underlying engine. src/index.ts renames claudeResponse to mannyResponse and updates CLI prompts.

eli5.text: The helper built into the code editor now calls itself 'Manny' instead of 'assistant' in its conversations and written instructions, so when you talk to it, the program identifies itself by name. When the Manny helper tells you what files it changed, it says 'based on Manny's instruction,' and if it gets confused about which files it has already looked at, it will skip re-reading those same files again to save time. Manny is powered by the AI engine behind Claude, according to the project notes.

ai.title: Fix duplicate file updates in promptClaudeAndGetFileChanges
ai.summary: Moved `parseFileBlocks` call outside the `while` loop in `backend/src/prompts.ts`. Prevents redundant processing of tool results on each iteration. Adjusted `currentFileBlock` clearing logic inside the stream chunk loop. Added debug logging to `processFileBlock`.

eli5.text: When the assistant was working on a task, it used to re-read and process the same set of file changes over and over with each step it took, like flipping back to the same page in a recipe while still cooking. Now it reads those file changes just once at the start, so each file update is applied cleanly instead of being repeated. You wouldn't see this directly, but if you watched the assistant working on your request, files would now update correctly the first time instead of being processed again on every loop.

ai.title: ChatStorage persists sessions in .manicode/chats
ai.summary: New `ChatStorage` class persists chat sessions as JSON files in `.manicode/chats`, replacing in-memory `messageHistory`. `src/index.ts` initializes storage per project root, creating chats with unique IDs and updating them on user/assistant messages. Added `.manicode` to `.gitignore` to exclude local chat data.

eli5.text: The assistant now saves your conversations so they stick around between sessions instead of disappearing when you close the program. Each chat you have gets stored as its own file in a local folder, and you’ll see a new chat ID printed when you start a conversation. Your chat history is now saved in the background automatically.

ai.title: prompts.ts: Fallback file change record when diff empty
ai.summary: Added fallback logic in `processFileBlock` to push a change record with original content if `changes` array remains empty. Prevents silent omission of file state when regex-based diff detection yields no matches. Scope limited to `backend/src/prompts.ts`. Mechanism ensures `changes` always contains at least one entry for processed files, overriding subsequent `updatedContent === oldContent` check.

eli5.text: When the system tries to update a file but finds no actual changes to record, it now writes a default entry noting that the file was checked and kept as-is, rather than silently skipping it. This affects internal tooling that tracks which files were reviewed during automated processes. If you looked at the change log, you'd see that previously some files could be left unmentioned when nothing changed, but now every file gets a clear record of being processed.

ai.title: System prompt instructs to update knowledge.md on user corrections
ai.summary: Added instruction to `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` directing the agent to update `knowledge.md` files when users identify mistakes. This ensures recurring errors are documented as concise rules to prevent repetition. The change applies to the core system prompt logic.

eli5.text: When you point out that I made a mistake, I now write down the lesson so I don't repeat it. I do this in a running notes file in the folder where the error happened. Over time these notes turn into a concise guide covering the tricky parts of that area, so future help you get there builds on what we already learned, instead of starting from scratch.

ai.title: ChatStorage generateChatId uses date-time format
ai.summary: ChatStorage.generateChatId replaces random Date.now() base36 ID with ISO date-time string YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS plus random suffix. Improves chat file name readability and sorting. Internal storage mechanism change in src/chat-storage.ts. Existing random IDs remain valid.

eli5.text: Chats saved on your device now get file names that start with the date and time they were created, like "2024-07-16_14-30-22_abc12", instead of a random string of letters and numbers. If you ever browse your saved chats, you\'ll be able to tell when each one happened just by reading the name. Any chats you already have are untouched and still open normally. This only affects how new chats are named behind the scenes.
